findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed several dented cans on the shelves. The cans were removed from service and the PIC was educated. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect the integrity of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) The debris underneath the glass portion behind the Jolly Rancher frozen beverage machine nozzles.

(2) The debris behind the slushy machine nozzles.

(3) The dust and other debris on the shelves inside the walk-in drink cooler. 

(4) The debris behind the cappuccino machine nozzles. 

(5) The surface above the coffee pot. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris, dust, and other residues. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a leak at the triple sink faucet. Ensure that the leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is not a covered waste receptacle in the female toilet room for sanitary napkins. Ensure that the female toilet room has a covered waste receptacle by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION:
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions.  The facility is observed to have soiled floors and shelving due to a previous mouse infestation. Originally noted in the 2023 inspection, evidence of current presence was observed throughout the facility. During today’s inspection, there is observed mouse droppings throughout the entire back storage area (from around the soda service station to the opposite alcohol and office space). There are not any large numbers. And droppings appear to be old. There was also an old dead mouse under the soda boxes. This is a cleaning issue. Cleaning will need to be extensive and thorough. Remove all the bulk boxes of sundries from the back storage space and clean the floor. SCDPH will allow thirty days for compliance to allow for detail cleaning. As part of cleaning, see that the walls around the soda syrup storage shelf are cleaned and painted as required. Soda splash is observed around the wall behind the syrup boxes and on the ceiling above the shelf. 
Finally, the floor drain of the hand sink behind the soda service station is observed soiled with mold growth.
Clean the aforementioned areas paying particular attention to the soda syrup storage area. 

 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. The back room is observed to have damage to several ceiling tiles directly over the soda syrup box shelf. The ceiling tiles should be replaced and best practice would be to use a vinyl coated tile - to allow for proper cleaning. In addition to the cleaning to address the previous pest problem (see other 55 violation) maintenance should be conducted to insure surfaces are properly sealed to prevent entrance of pests. There are observed several holes in walls around the alcohol storage across from the office space and around the soda syrup boxes. As you clean, seal any observed holes with steel wool. The use of spray foam is allowed, but mice will chew through this material. 
Furthermore, several of the acoustic tiles in the back storage room are observed water stained from water damage. Replace the ceiling tiles with ones that are in good repair.

The wall holding the shelving with mouse droppings is observed to have mold and mildew damage. Discussed using a Kilz or similar product to seal the wall to prevent further growth. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The facility has been cited for multiple priority/priority foundation violations AND has conditions which have created an imminent health hazard resulting in the immediate suspension of food service permit. As such, active managerial control has not been demonstrated by the person-in-charge of the facility. Inspector will return on both 1/22/2023 AND 6/21/2023 to evaluate compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code requirements.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink in the facility was not stocked with paper towels nor hand soap during the inspection. Hand sinks must be stocked and accessible at all times to facilitate proper hand washing and prevent contamination. Inspector will return on 1/1/2024 to ensure that the hand sink is properly stocked and accessible. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The triple sink at the rear of the facility is used to wash personal items and as a dump sink. The triple sink is provided with paper towels via a paper towel dispenser on the wall and hand soap via a hand soap dispenser on the wall. The triple sink is NOT to be used for hand washing and MAY NOT be equipped with handwashing aids/devices intended for hand washing sinks. Ensure that these devices are removed and that hand washing is occurring at the hand sink as required.

6-301.13: A sink used for FOOD preparation or UTENSIL washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a HANDWASHING SINK.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Several packages of chips were observed to be open and exposed to contamination by pests in the facility. These opened packages of chips were observed sitting in a shallow plastic display container with a thin wooden bottom which had an approximately quarter size hole in the bottom of it. Rodent droppings were observed in the area the foods were stored. Additionally, inspector observed boxes of sweetener packets in a cabinet with mouse droppings and dead insects in the box. These items must be discarded immediately. Single-service items in the plastic holder on the coffee counter are observed to be sitting on surfaces contaminated with mouse droppings. Items in this holder include sweetener packets and single-service coffee creamers. These items must be discarded immediately as well. A follow-up is issued for 12/26/2023 to check for additional contamination. Foods which are contaminated must be discarded and not offered for service. Ensure that foods are checked regularly for evidence of pest penetration into the packaging and that contaminated foods are IMMEDIATELY discarded.

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed several areas of concern in the back room where the triple sink and soda are stored. Under the triple sink, inspector observed a dead mouse amongst many droppings and nesting material. To the right of the dead mouse was a hole approximately 2 inches wide and 3/4 of an inch tall where mice have been able to enter and exit the room. Near the soda boxes, inspector observed large amounts of soda syrup splashed on the floor, walls, ceiling and ceiling vents. In this area, x3 dead and decaying mouse corpses were observed. One of the three was stuck to an old, heavily soiled glue trap. One was stuck to the back of the right-rear leg of the soda shelving. And the third was on the floor under the shelving. Enormous amounts of mouse droppings were observed on these shelves and at the floor/wall junction in these areas. A drain in the area was heavily soiled with residue/debris and mouse droppings. A dead mouse was also observed behind numerous stacked boxes of liquor along with mouse droppings too numerous to count near the rodent corpse and along the floor/wall junction in this area.

Due to these observations, inspector contacted the SCDPH Environmental Health Director (AA) and requested additional assistance with enforcement. AA arrived at the facility. Inspector AM arrived shortly after. 

AA spoke with operator. Operator stated that pest control is present on a monthly basis. A report was provided from 12/8/2023 which showed that pest control was presented and treated for multiple pests/insects including the placement of glue traps and bait.

Inspector pointed out additional areas of concern including numerous shelves, boxes and countertops with mouse droppings observed in both the back room and the section behind the soda counter where the soda fountain drain is located. At this time, due to the severity of the rodent infestation within the facility, SCDPH Environmental Health Director (AA) informed the operator that the facilities permit to serve food is being suspended effective immediately until the pest problem is under control and cleaning has occurred. Facility may continue to serve fully pre-packaged foods but the soda fountain, slushy machines, and coffee machines MAY NOT be used until approval is granted by SCDPH. Operator is to contact third-party PCO and contact SCDPH inspector to ensure that inspector can be there for planning and/or discuss plans with the PCO. Inspector will return on 12/26/2023 to evaluate progress and discuss plans for elimination of pests within the facility.

Additional mouse droppings, insects and harborage conditions were observed ubiquitously throughout the rest of the facility.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
The near ubiquitous presence of dead mice and mouse droppings throughout the facility represent significant forms of contamination for all foods stored within the facility. Additionally, mold, dust and other residue/debris was observed on shelving and on top of boxes food/drink are stored in. Cabinets used to store food and single use/service items are observed to have soil and mouse droppings present. It is recommended that facility invest in plastic containers to prevent contamination of foods and single use/service items in the future. Facility must ensure that areas where food and single use/service items are stored remain clean, free of pests/droppings, and that all such items are protected from ANY source of contamination during storage. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Tongs were stored in the bottom drawer of the hot-dog roller which is not current being used. The drawer had several mouse droppings present. Ensure that clean utensils stored in the facility are protected from sources of contamination including but not limited to mouse droppings. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed single-use cups stored in a cabinet with large amounts of mouse droppings present along with an active bait trap. Both the droppings and bait trap are sources of hazardous contamination. All single-use cups in these cabinets must be discarded immediately. Ensure that single service/single use items are protected from contamination at all times. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Equipment such as the slushy machines, soda machine, coffee machine, and hot-dog roller are observed to have mouse droppings and/or residue/debris accumulations present. The back of the right (from the front) slushy machine has a filter which is completely blocked with dust and other debris. The hot dog roller has numerous mouse droppings in the pan under the rollers.  All non-food contact surfaces of equipment must remain free of ANY accumulations at ALL times. Ensure that these surfaces are cleaned and remain clean.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
The faucet at the triple sink is observed to be leaking at the time of inspection. Ensure that the triple sink faucet is repaired so that the sink may be shut off completely and that plumbing remains in good repair during operations. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
Waste receptacles behind the facility are observed to be heavily soiled. The areas around these receptacles are heavily soiled with refuse and other residue/debris. Ensure that these areas and the receptacles are cleaned often enough to prevent such buildup. 

5-501.116: (A) Receptacles and waste handling units shall be cleaned in way to prevent contamination. (B) Receptacles and waste handling units shall be cleaned at frequency to prevent buildup.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several areas which are subject to food/water splash that are not SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE. Exposed drywall behind soda storage and under cabinets has been observed. Multiple areas throughout the facility have base coving which has begun to peel away from the wall, has been destroyed by mice, and/or is missing entirely. Acoustic ceiling tile in the back warewashing/storage area must be made easily cleanable. The hand sink has no caulking and is not otherwise sealed to clean behind it and must be sealed to the wall. Ensure that all areas subject to food/moisture meet the criteria of being SMOOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling tile along the east walk-in/display cooler is collapsing onto the top of the cooler. These ceiling tile must be attached so they are easily cleanable. Damaged tile must be replaced or otherwise sealed to provide a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface. 

6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Numerous floor/wall junctures in the facility are observed to have large gaps which allow entry of pests into the facility. These areas have been pointed out to person-in-charge during the inspection today. Areas include but are not limited to under the triple sink, behind the upright cooler near the hand sink, and behind and to the right of the coffee counter. Other areas likely exist that were not directly observed during the inspection due to excessive clutter. Ensure that all wall/floor junctures are coved, closed and sealed. 

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Multiple pieces of equipment that are not in use are retained in the facility. There is a large upright cooler and the roller grille along the east wall of the facility. Neither of these items are operational and the roller grill is not to be used based on the facilities current risk level which was downgraded approximately two years ago during the previous routine inspection. Neither piece of equipment remains clean to sight and touch and both have mouse droppings observed on/in them. This equipment and any other unused equipment must be removed from the premises.

6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The entire facility is heavily soiled with residue, debris, mouse droppings, dead mice, dead insects, dust, pest fur/dander, and other soil. A thorough deep cleaning is required to be completed throughout all areas of the facility. All stored items must be moved and cleaned behind. Clutter must be removed and/or otherwise consolidated in a manner that facilitate cleaning the facility. There are too many boxes and other items cluttering the facility that making cleaning near impossible on a routine basis. Ensure that the facility is cleaned and remains clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Observed mops stored in a position that did not allow it to drip/air dry. The mop was stored inside the top part of the mop bucket. Inspector moved the mop to a position that allowed it to air dry.
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: Observed no CFM in facility. However, See comment. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed soda machine ice dispenser and ice-e machine to have black residue. Clean dispensers as needed to prevent build-up. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed (L) W-I Cooler to be unable to maintain food 41F or below. Hot Dog (probed at 53-in between 2 packages) and milk (probed at 53F) were out of temperature. All TCS Foods will be discarded. This includes milk, hot dogs, and lunchables (containing meat). Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).
